item.title: One-China principle unshakable, DPP's "Taiwan independence" attempts doomed to fail: experts
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The recent meeting between the heads of state of China and the United States and the China-Russia-U.S. summit have sent a clear message: the Taiwan question is at the heart of China's core interests and the international community's commitment to the one-China principle is unshakable, experts and scholars across the Taiwan Strait said.
They said the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities' attempts to seek "Taiwan independence" by relying on external forces and military buildup are doomed to fail.
On Nov. 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping met with U.S. President Donald Trump, who was in the southern Chinese metropolis of Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting. Xi also hosted a historic summit with Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the same day.
During his meeting with Trump, Xi said that on the Taiwan question, the U.S. side should keep doing the right thing and avoid major setbacks in China-U.S. relations. Trump, for his part, said the United States does not support "Taiwan independence."
Chen Guiqing, a research fellow at the Beijing-based Institute of Taiwan Studies, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, said Xi had once again made China's firm position on the Taiwan question clear to the United States while also setting out China's expectations.
The Taiwan question concerns not only the overall stability of China-U.S. relations but also global stability, Chen said. Doing the right thing means, among other things, that the United States should stop playing the "Taiwan card" and refrain from sending wrong signals to secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," he said. Otherwise, it will affect efforts by the two countries to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability, Chen added.
Ni Yongjie, director of the Shanghai Institute of Taiwan Studies, noted that this was the first time during Trump's presidency that he had publicly stated at a meeting between the two heads of state that the United States does not support "Taiwan independence."
The statement represented a response by the U.S. side to China's major concerns over the Taiwan question, Ni said.
Experts said the Taiwan-related positions articulated by the two leaders dealt another heavy blow to secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence."
Chang Chun-kai, a research fellow at the Center for Cross-Strait Political and Economic Studies, Chengchi University, said the one-China principle constitutes the political foundation of China-U.S. relations and is indispensable to ensuring peace and stability.
Peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait depend on the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, Chang said, adding that this is also in line with the broader trend toward a stable relationship between China and the United States.
The Taiwan question stems from China's civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC.
The unresolved civil war, combined with foreign interference, has kept the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed.
At the trilateral meeting with Putin and Trump, Xi stressed that countries should not interfere in one another's domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs. On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another's perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another, Xi said.
Putin said the three countries should adhere to the principles of sovereign equality and noninterference in internal affairs, and look for ways to resolve concerns in a balanced manner through cooperation.
Li Huan, a research fellow at the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations, said the summit carries an important message for the Taiwan question: major countries are willing to sit down and communicate directly to manage differences and avoid misjudgment and conflict, which shatters the attempt and illusion of secessionist forces to exploit competition among major countries to pursue "Taiwan independence."
Commenting on Trump's statement and the consensus reached by the three heads of state, Chen said that although secessionist forces on the island are trying to downplay their significance, more and more people in Taiwan will come to see clearly that "Taiwan independence" attempts find no support and will never succeed.
Xi noted at the summit that, as the main victors of World War II, China, Russia and the United States should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and defend the hard-won outcomes of victory in World War II.
Li said Taiwan's restoration to China was one of the outcomes of victory in World War II and an important part of the postwar international order, adding that the historical and legal fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China is clear and indisputable.
By recalling the three countries' history of fighting side by side during World War II and reaffirming their commitment to safeguarding the postwar international order and the purposes of the UN Charter, the summit sent a stern warning to forces seeking to challenge that order and undermine the achievements of the war, including secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," she said.
Feng Wang, a Taiwan-based history writer, said the history of World War II and the victory over fascism were shared historical memories of the international community that must neither be forgotten nor distorted.
People in Taiwan should not be misled by political manipulation or erroneous views of history, Wang said, adding that people from all walks of life in Taiwan should take a long-term and broad view, thinking in the direction that benefits Taiwan compatriots, the country and the Chinese nation.
"Secession aimed at 'Taiwan independence' is the root cause of turmoil across the Taiwan Strait. It harms the immediate interests of people on both sides of the Strait and is widely opposed by the international community. It is a dead end," Ni said.
The DPP authorities should abandon their secessionist stance as soon as possible and return to the path of peaceful development of cross-Strait relations, he added.

item.title: Launch site ready for China's Shenzhou-24 spaceflight mission
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
This photo taken on Nov. 17, 2026 shows the combination of the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft and a Long March-2F carrier rocket being transferred to the launch area. (Photo by Ge Lixin/Xinhua)
JIUQUAN, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The launch site for China's Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceflight mission has completed all preparations, with equipment, personnel and systems ready.
The Shenzhou-24 mission completed its final full-system joint rehearsal on Saturday, marking the last such exercise before liftoff. The rocket, spacecraft and all systems of the launch site are in good condition, according to the launch site.
Functional checks, joint tests and propellant loading will proceed as scheduled ahead of the launch.
On Nov. 17, the combination of the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft and its Long March-2F carrier rocket was transferred to the launch area.

item.title: Guarding green rainforest in China's southernmost province
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
A drone photo taken on Sept. 10, 2026 shows a view of the Wuzhishan section of the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park in south China's Hainan Province. (Xinhua/Pu Xiaoxu)
HAIKOU, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- Early in the morning, the mountainous rainforest of Wuzhishan in south China's Hainan Province is still shrouded in thick clouds and mist.
Wang Cheng opens the "Rainforest Patrol" application on his phone, gets on his motorcycle and sets off for his patrol mission through the mountains. As he travels, his route is automatically recorded on an electronic map.
Wang's family has lived at the foot of these mountains for generations, and the 44-year-old ethnic Li forest ranger treats the forests of his hometown as old friends, deserving of constant care and protection.
Decades ago, local villagers depended heavily on the mountains for their livelihoods. Logging and slash-and-burn farming had fragmented parts of the rainforest.
In 2021, China established its first five national parks, including the National Park of Hainan Tropical Rainforest. Since then, protecting the rainforest has become a shared responsibility, extending beyond the work of government departments and researchers to local communities. Many villagers inside the park have transitioned into forest ranger roles, with Wang being one of them.
This photo taken on Sept. 9, 2026 shows a stream at the Diaoluoshan section of the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park in south China's Hainan Province. (Xinhua/Pu Xiaoxu)
The transformation of Hainan's rainforest is once again in the international spotlight as the province hosts the ongoing 2026 Tropical Rainforest Ecosystem Partners Conference. The event, underway in the provincial capital Haikou, has brought together international officials, experts and representatives from more than 20 countries to exchange views on rainforest conservation and sustainable development.
Discussions have covered water conservation and ecological security, biodiversity protection, the development and utilization of forest food resources, mechanisms for realizing the value of ecological products, cultural heritage preservation and rainforest carbon governance.
International speakers at the conference highlighted the global importance of rainforest conservation, emphasizing its close links with food security, climate resilience and human well-being.
A think tank report titled "A Great Song Resounds in the Rainforest: The 'Hainan Model' of China's Tropical Rainforest Conservation" was released at the event, examining Hainan's experience in protecting its tropical rainforest ecosystem.
Hainan's tropical rainforest is the most concentrated, best-preserved and largest contiguous continental-island-type tropical rainforest in China, and forms an important part of the world's tropical rainforest system. Over the years, authorities have stepped up efforts to protect its valuable natural heritage.
The results are increasingly visible on the ground. On his patrols, Wang often spots tree crabs, which are indicators of a healthy rainforest ecosystem. Infrared cameras also frequently capture images of rare birds and animals.
Behind these observations is a "space-air-ground integrated" monitoring network operating within the park, combining satellite remote sensing, drones, acoustic monitoring devices and on-the-ground ranger patrols.
"When I see these creatures living and thriving peacefully, I know this forest has truly come back to life," Wang said.
The wildlife recovery reflects a whole set of systematic governance reforms. The National Park of Hainan Tropical Rainforest consolidated more than 20 previously scattered protected areas, relying on natural restoration supplemented by moderate artificial restoration to safeguard the rainforest's integrity.
The province has also completed China's first natural-resource ownership registration for a national park, taking stock of its forests, wetlands and water resources. Authorities orderly completed the ecological relocation of 459 households totaling 1,975 people from the core protected zone of the park.
Yet the challenges facing tropical rainforests extend far beyond Hainan.
The ongoing strong El Niño phenomenon is pushing the world's tropical rainforests to the brink of crisis. Rising forest fire risks, disturbed wildlife habitats and disrupted ecological water cycles continue to plague many tropical countries, where the tension between ecological protection and livelihood development persists.
"China's tropical rainforest management is already quite comprehensive," said Maria Rosda Lima Panggur, forest ecosystem manager at Komodo National Park in Indonesia, speaking at the conference.
The report not only profiles the biodiversity information, but also includes the cultural heritage -- how local communities relate to nature -- as well as conservation management and a big part of technology, such as smart patrols and monitoring, according to her.
"I think it's really a great effort for biodiversity conservation," she added.
For Wang, however, the challenges of rainforest conservation are increasingly apparent. El Niño has brought prolonged high temperatures and drought, adding to the daily pressure of forest management. During his patrols, he must now keep an even closer watch for fire risks and closely monitor the effects of dry weather on the survival of plants and animals.
"We guard the mountains, and the mountains guard us," he said.

item.title: Why China-Russia-U.S. summit hailed historic for world stability, peace
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)
BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- World leaders and observers spoke highly of the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States, saying the talks have brought the world hope for peace, stability and cooperation.
Chinese President Xi Jinping chaired the historic summit in the city of Shenzhen, south China, on Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump.
As major countries and permanent members of the UN Security Council, China, Russia and the United States should set good examples, work together to meet global challenges, jointly uphold world peace and stability, and make greater contributions to the progress of humanity, Xi said.
Following the summit, the three countries released the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, outlining their common understandings on issues including the UN reform, energy security, the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court and nuclear risk reduction.
LANDMARK STEP FOR GLOBAL SECURITY
At a White House news conference on Friday, Trump hailed the Shenzhen meeting as "one of the most momentous international summits in many years." He said the "historic summit" had produced a trilateral peace declaration in which China, Russia and the United States reaffirmed that a nuclear war must never be fought.
Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said China's efforts to host the summit will help create and open up space for meaningful dialogue and mutual understanding toward lasting peace and harmony.
Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said the three leaders had shown wisdom and statesmanship in taking a step that mattered to the wider international community.
Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico said he noticed how often the leaders had spoken of peace during their meeting.
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi)
At the United Nations, Farhan Haq, deputy spokesman for the secretary-general, said the organization welcomed efforts by world leaders, including those of the Security Council's permanent members, to seek common solutions to global problems.
Denis Simon, former executive vice chancellor of Duke Kunshan University, said the summit could open a new channel for dialogue on international security among the three countries whose decisions carry considerable military, economic and diplomatic weight.
"I see the meeting as an important opening," said Paul Frimpong, executive director of the Africa-China Center for Policy and Advisory. With several international crises unfolding at once, he said, sitting together gave each leader a chance to hear directly from the other two about the risks they considered most pressing and where they saw room to act together.
Gergely Salat, a senior researcher at the Hungarian Institute of International Affairs, said the meeting showed that China has been maintaining channels with both Washington and Moscow and has enough credibility with both to bring them to the same table. "Few capitals could do that today," he said.
FINDING RIGHT WAY TO GET ALONG
At the summit, Xi made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace, calling for mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation.
"China, Russia and the United States should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means," he said.
Sourabh Gupta, a resident senior fellow at the Institute for China-America Studies in Washington, noted the repeated references at the summit to preserving the outcomes of World War II. As permanent members of the UN Security Council, the three countries bear a special responsibility for maintaining international peace and security, he said.
Wang Yiwei, a professor at Renmin University of China's School of International Studies, said advances in artificial intelligence were adding a new layer of risk for nuclear powers. Against that backdrop, he said, China's emphasis on preserving strategic stability at the summit sent an encouraging signal about the prospects for peace.
Shraga Biran, head of Israel's Institute for Structural Reforms, pointed to the Middle East, noting that with several regional flashpoints in play, reliable communication can keep one miscalculation from triggering another and reduce the risk that a crisis escalates by accident.
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 19, 2026. (Xinhua/Shen Hong)
ENCOURAGING CONSENSUS
Xi called on the three countries to follow through on the consensus reached at the summit, strengthen communication, build common ground through dialogue, promote peace via cooperation, and work together to build a better world.
Ezzat Saad, director of the Cairo-based Egyptian Council for Foreign Affairs, said that a better understanding among the major countries could give diplomats more room to work and help contain tensions across the Middle East region.
"When fuel and freight costs rise, businesses pay more to move goods, and families can feel it in food prices," said Frimpong with the Africa-China Center for Policy and Advisory.
In the heads of state declaration released following the summit, the three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows.
In regions recovering from conflict, Frimpong said, more reliable energy supplies would also make it easier for businesses to reopen and invest.
For Alphonse Muleefu, principal of the College of Arts and Social Sciences at the University of Rwanda, the declaration issued in Shenzhen showed that the three countries could find common ground. Building on it, he said, would take mutual respect, sustained dialogue and practical cooperation.
"I believe this meeting marks an encouraging step toward a more stable world," he said.

item.title: Forum on overseas studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era held in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-22
Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 21, 2026. (Xinhua/Pang Xinglei)
BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era opened in Beijing on Saturday.
Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony.
Participants said Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era had taken shape and evolved through efforts to respond to questions posed by China, by the world, by the people, and by the times, and to advance China's development in tandem with that of the rest of the world.
They noted that Xi has proposed the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity, offering China's answer to common challenges facing countries in the current era and has won broad recognition from the international community.
Participants called for stronger overseas research into and communication of the Thought, as well as joint efforts to advance global development, safeguard world peace and stability, promote human progress and improve the global governance system.
Under the theme "The Great Way: Building a Community with a Shared Future for Humanity," the forum was hosted by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
It will run through Sunday, with thematic sessions also being held in Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and five countries, namely Uzbekistan, Ethiopia, Greece, Hungary and Uruguay, bringing together nearly 650 participants from more than 80 countries and regions.

item.title: Shenzhen 'peace summit' underscores shared responsibilities of major countries
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
BEIJING, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- The first-ever face-to-face meeting between the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States in Shenzhen sent a clear message at a time of mounting geopolitical tensions: the world needs major countries to build bridges, not barriers, and safeguard peace, not fuel confrontation.
The historic meeting on Nov. 19, which Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi described as a "peace summit," saw the three leaders engage in candid, friendly and constructive exchanges on major issues concerning global peace, security and stability. It also produced a series of important consensuses and a declaration toward peace, demonstrating that even countries with differences can find common ground through dialogue.
Yet some have sought to frame the meeting as "Yalta 2.0," drawing a flawed parallel with the 1945 gathering of the leaders of the Soviet Union, the United States and Britain that helped shape the postwar order. Such readings are rooted in the old mindset of power politics and spheres of influence, and ignore profound shifts in the global landscape.
The circumstances and choices facing the world today are fundamentally different. The Shenzhen meeting was not about deciding the fate of other countries behind closed doors. Rather, it focused on how three major countries, despite their differences, could strengthen communication, manage disagreements and jointly safeguard peace and stability.
Chinese President Xi Jinping made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace, calling for mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation. Together, they offer a constructive path for fostering sound major-country relations in a turbulent world.
Mutual respect and peaceful coexistence should be firmly upheld. Nations differ in their social systems, histories, cultures and development paths. Such differences are an objective reality of international relations, not a license for confrontation or interference. No country should seek to impose its will on others, still less treat another country's legitimate development as a threat simply because it is growing stronger.
Win-win cooperation is a practical necessity in a deeply interconnected world, rather than a mere diplomatic slogan. Global supply chains, trade and technological innovation link countries in ways that cannot be easily undone without imposing costs on all sides. Attempts to decouple economies, disrupt supply chains or erect barriers to technological cooperation may serve narrow geopolitical calculations, but they inevitably undermine shared development and weaken the foundations of global prosperity.
No country can secure its own long-term development by denying others' legitimate right to develop. The choice before major countries is not between one country's success and another's, but between pursuing shared progress and allowing zero-sum rivalry to hold everyone back.
Dialogue and consultation are equally indispensable. Major countries inevitably have differences, some of them deep and long-standing. The measure of responsible diplomacy is not whether these differences can be eliminated overnight, but whether they can be managed properly without escalating into confrontation. Maintaining regular high-level exchanges, keeping communication channels open and strengthening crisis-prevention mechanisms are therefore not optional gestures, but essential safeguards against miscalculation and conflict.
This is particularly important because major countries bear far-reaching responsibilities. When major countries live in harmony, the world is at peace; when they fight, the world is thrown into turmoil. Their interactions affect not only bilateral ties, but also regional security, the global economy and prospects for peace across the world.
China's vision of an equal and orderly multipolar world reflects this conviction. It's a world in which countries, regardless of size or strength, enjoy equal opportunities to participate in international affairs, differences are addressed through consultation rather than coercion, and international rules and institutions are upheld by all to serve the common interests of the international community.
Viewed from this broader perspective, the significance of the Shenzhen meeting becomes clear. It did not erase the differences among the three countries, nor could a single meeting resolve every international challenge. Instead, its value lies in reaffirming the importance of sustained communication, identifying areas of common ground and creating more room for managing differences. At a time when mistrust and confrontation threaten to narrow the space for diplomacy, that is no small achievement.
The world has already learned, at great cost, where division, confrontation and power politics can lead. What it needs now is not another attempt to carve up spheres of influence, but the political courage of major countries to respect one another, coexist peacefully and pursue the common interests of all humanity.
The consensus reached by the three leaders should be translated into concrete actions to build a future shaped by dialogue, mutual respect and shared responsibility.

item.title: Asia-Pacific Media Partnership officially launched
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The Asia-Pacific Media Partnership (APMP), proposed by China's Xinhua News Agency, has been officially launched, with its first batch of members comprising 310 organizations from 41 countries and regions across the Asia-Pacific.
At the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Media Forum held on Sept. 5, more than 400 representatives from over 40 countries and regions, as well as from UN agencies and international organizations, witnessed the establishment of the Organizing Committee of the Asia-Pacific Media Partnership Program.
The committee issued an initiative on strengthening collaborative communication between the media and think tanks, inviting media outlets and think tanks in the Asia-Pacific region to join the partnership.
Aiming to strengthen mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation among media organizations across the Asia-Pacific region, the APMP focuses on building four key platforms: high-end dialogue, collaborative communication, technological innovation and pragmatic cooperation.
It will regularly hold high-level media dialogues, promote joint interviews among Asia-Pacific media, jointly produce high-quality multimedia products, organize inbound reporting tours in China for Asia-Pacific media journalists, and host themed training programs for Asia-Pacific media professionals, among a series of practical cooperation projects.
Both the APMP and the Shenzhen Consensus of the Asia-Pacific Media Forum have been officially included in the deliverables list for China's hosting of the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meetings. The Asia-Pacific Media Forum has also been included in the list of meetings and events hosted by China as the 2026 APEC host.

item.title: Trump calls trilateral summit with Xi, Putin one of most momentous in years
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
WASHINGTON, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday hailed his "unprecedented" trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin as one of the most significant international meetings in years.
"We had one of the most momentous international summits in many years. That was the first ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China," Trump told a press conference at the White House. "And the relationship was fantastic between the three of us."
"The result of this historic summit was a first-of-its-kind trilateral peace declaration," Trump said. "The United States, Russia and China formally agreed that nuclear conflict must never be allowed to happen."
Trump also described the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, as "very successful."
At the trilateral summit in Shenzhen on Thursday, the three leaders had an in-depth exchange of views on maintaining world peace and promoting strategic stability in major country relations. Following the summit, the three countries released the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace.
